h1: B2 English for ILR: the higher level starts on 26 March 2027
intro: The English level needed for settlement is rising. Under changes already made to the Immigration Rules, most people will need B2 English for ILR applications made from 26 March 2027, up from B1 now. Here’s who it affects, how B2 differs from B1, and whether applying earlier could help you.

sections.heading: What’s changing
sections.text:
At the moment, most people applying for Indefinite Leave to Remain must show English at B1 level in speaking and listening. The Statement of Changes HC 1691, laid in March 2026, raises this to B2 for settlement applications made on or after 26 March 2027.

The government confirmed in its earned settlement announcement on 2 November 2026 that a high standard of English will be a core requirement for settlement in future.

sections.heading: Who needs B2 English for ILR?
sections.text:
The new level applies to people applying for settlement on routes where English is required, such as Skilled Worker, partner and other work routes. The usual exemptions continue:
- people aged 65 or over
- people with a long-term physical or mental condition that prevents them meeting the requirement
- nationals of majority English-speaking countries
- people with a degree taught in English, confirmed by Ecctis if it’s from outside the UK

The changes announced so far apply to settlement. We’ll update this page if the requirement for British citizenship changes.

sections.heading: How B2 differs from B1
sections.text:
B1 is intermediate: you can deal with everyday situations and talk about familiar topics. B2 is upper-intermediate: you can follow complex discussions, speak fluently with native speakers and explain your views in detail.

For many people, moving from B1 to B2 takes several months of study. Try our free [B2 English test practice](/b2-english-test-practice/) to see where you are now, or our [B1 practice test](/b1-english-test-practice/) if you’re applying before the change.

sections.heading: Should you apply before 26 March 2027?
sections.text:
If you’ll meet all the settlement requirements before 26 March 2027, applying before that date means B1 is enough. But the qualifying period for settlement is also changing under the earned settlement reforms, which will be brought in during 2027. Don’t rush an application that isn’t ready, as a refusal costs the fee and can affect future applications.

If you’re close to qualifying, get advice now so you can plan around both changes.

sections.heading: Proving your English
sections.text: You can prove your English with a Secure English Language Test (SELT) from a Home Office approved provider, at the right level. A test pass is usually valid for two years for a new application. Book early: test centres can get busy when a rule change is coming. Read our full guide to the [English language requirement](/english-language-requirement/).

sections.heading: How we can help
sections.text: We can check whether you meet the English requirement or an exemption, when you’ll qualify for settlement, and whether applying before the change makes sense. [Contact us](/contact-us/) to book a consultation.

faqs.q: When does B2 English for ILR start?
faqs.a: For settlement applications made on or after 26 March 2027.

faqs.q: What level do I need if I apply before then?
faqs.a: B1 in speaking and listening, as now, unless you’re exempt.

faqs.q: Does the change affect British citizenship?
faqs.a: The changes announced so far apply to settlement. We’ll update this page if the citizenship requirement changes.

faqs.q: Can I use my old B1 test for ILR after March 2027?
faqs.a: Not if the new rules require B2. You would need a B2 pass or another accepted way of proving your English.

faqs.q: Which test do I need for B2 English for ILR?
faqs.a: A Secure English Language Test at B2 or above from a Home Office approved provider. Check the approved list on GOV.UK before you book, as other tests aren’t accepted.
